To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we have used gene knock-in technology to generate mice expressing either the wild-type human apoA-I gene or the human apoA-IM gene, (2) we have shown that apoA-IM expression in mice is associated with reduced plasma levels of the apolipoprotein, and (3) we have demonstrated that reduced apoA-IM plasma levels in mice are due, at least in part, to reduced apoA- IM synthesis and secretion by the liver.

(1) we have generated mice that express either human apoA-IM or human apoA-I; (2) we have shown that the expression of the human apoproteins is not different between A-IM and A-I mice; and (3) we have shown, for the first time in vivo, that the expression of apoA- IM is associated with impaired apoA-1 secretion.
the hypoalphaproteinemia associated with apoA-IM is due to a defect in apoA- IM secretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new mouse model for the study of apoA-Imilano and its role in the pathogenesis of atherosclerosis.
the development of a new model of human atherosclerosis.
the development of animal models that will allow the study of the mechanisms by which apoA-I and apoAI-Milano modulate lipid metabolism.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the apoA-1 Milano variant, in contrast to apoA-1, is not secreted at the same rate by hepatocytes.
the A-IM gene k-in mice provide an excellent model to study the molecular basis of hypoalphalipoprotenemia associated with the A-IM mutation.
the hypoalphaproteinemia observed in apoA-Imilano carriers is due to the impaired synthesis and/or secretion of the human apoA-IM protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully generated mouse lines expressing either human apoA-IM or human apoA-I in a controlled manner.
we have developed the first animal model to study the mechanisms of hypoalphaproteinemia associated with human carriers of apoA-Imutants.

1) the hypoalphalipoproteinemia associated with apoA-IM in human carriers is partially explained by reduced apoA-IM synthesis and secretion; and 2) the gene targeting technology is a useful approach to study the molecular mechanisms of human disease in a controlled manner.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the hypoalphapolipoproteinemia observed in human carriers of the R173C mutation of apoA-I is due to a reduced rate of apoA- IM secretion.
the apoA-1Milano mutation is associated with impaired apoA-I secretion.
the apoA-Imutant has a reduced rate of secretion from the liver.
